lba_qa.q: A water tank is in the shape of a cylinder with radius 7 m and height 10 m. Find how much water it can hold (volume). (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Volume of a cylinder = pi x r^2 x h.
= (22/7) x 7 x 7 x 10 = 22 x 7 x 10 = 1540 cubic metres.
So the tank can hold 1540 cubic metres of water.

lba_qa.q: A cricket ball is a sphere of radius 3.5 cm. Find its volume. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Volume of a sphere = (4/3) x pi x r^3.
= (4/3) x (22/7) x 3.5 x 3.5 x 3.5.
3.5^3 = 42.875.
= (4/3) x (22/7) x 42.875 = (4/3) x 134.75 = 179.67 cubic cm (approx).
So the volume of the ball is about 179.67 cubic cm.

lba_qa.q: An ice cream cone has radius 3.5 cm and height 12 cm. Find the volume of ice cream it can hold (cone volume). (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Volume of a cone = (1/3) x pi x r^2 x h.
= (1/3) x (22/7) x 3.5 x 3.5 x 12.
= (1/3) x (22/7) x 12.25 x 12 = (1/3) x 462 = 154 cubic cm.
So the cone can hold 154 cubic cm of ice cream.

lba_qa.q: A room is shaped like a cuboid measuring 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. Find the volume of air in the room.
lba_qa.a:
Volume of a cuboid = length x breadth x height.
= 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 cubic metres.
So the room holds 60 cubic metres of air.

lba_qa.q: A solid is made by placing a cone on top of a cylinder (like an ice cream in a cylindrical glass). How do we find the total volume of such a combined solid?
lba_qa.a: For a combined solid, we add the volumes of the individual shapes. Total volume = volume of cylinder + volume of cone = (pi r^2 h_cylinder) + (1/3 pi r^2 h_cone). We calculate each part separately using its formula and add them. This method of adding volumes is used for any solid made by combining basic shapes.

lba_qa.q: A cylindrical pillar has radius 0.5 m and height 7 m. Find the curved surface area to know how much paint is needed. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Curved surface area of a cylinder = 2 x pi x r x h.
= 2 x (22/7) x 0.5 x 7 = 2 x 22 x 0.5 = 22 square metres.
So 22 sq m of the pillar needs to be painted.

lba_qa.q: A metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into smaller spheres of radius 2 cm. How is the number of small spheres found? Explain the idea.
lba_qa.a:
When a solid is melted and recast, its total volume stays the same. So the number of small spheres = volume of big sphere / volume of one small sphere.
= [(4/3)pi(6)^3] / [(4/3)pi(2)^3] = 6^3/2^3 = 216/8 = 27.
So 27 small spheres can be made. The key idea is that the volume is conserved during melting and recasting.

lba_qa.q: A cube has each side 4 cm. Find its total surface area and volume.
lba_qa.a:
Total surface area of a cube = 6 x side^2 = 6 x 4 x 4 = 96 sq cm.
Volume of a cube = side^3 = 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 cubic cm.
So the surface area is 96 sq cm and the volume is 64 cubic cm.
lba_qa.topic: Surface area and volume of a cube

lba_qa.q: A hemispherical bowl has radius 7 cm. Find the volume of liquid it can hold. (Use pi = 22/7)
lba_qa.a:
Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3) x pi x r^3.
= (2/3) x (22/7) x 7 x 7 x 7 = (2/3) x 22 x 49 = (2/3) x 1078 = 718.67 cubic cm (approx).
So the bowl can hold about 718.67 cubic cm of liquid.

lba_qa.q: Why does a sphere of the same radius and height as a cylinder hold less volume than the cylinder? Explain conceptually.
lba_qa.a: A cylinder fills its full circular cross-section throughout its height, so it uses all the space in that region. A sphere curves inward at the top and bottom, leaving empty space near the corners of the same region. Because of this curving in, the sphere occupies less space than the cylinder of the same radius and height. That is why the sphere holds less volume.
